claims.author: purpleKarrot
claims.quote: Since the log function is global, there is no need for local user data. It can be a simple function pointer, even in the C++ wrapper.
claims.request: Drop local user_data in favor of a simple function pointer

status_by.quote: Forcing the user to use globals if they need state seems unnecessary, when using `user_data` is I think a well-established pattern in C APIs?

claims.status_note: author replied that user_data avoids forcing users to use globals for state

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.harm: Prematurely restricts the kernel logging API in a way difficult to reverse without notable simplification
claims.quote: I think it would be a mistake to limit functionality of the logging/debuging/tracing API prematurely, in a way that seems difficult to reverse and does not seem to provide a noticeable simplification

status_by.quote: I believe this new approach addresses your concern about callers having to restructure if logging is contextualized later, because the connection handle is kept.

claims.status_note: author force-pushed to keep btck_LoggingConnection handles while enforcing a single active connection to avoid caller restructuring

claims.author: sedited
claims.question: Does the pointer have to be a raw pointer?
claims.quote: Does this have to be a raw pointer?

status_by.quote: I think so, to avoid running consumer code from static destructors.

claims.status_note: author explained that a raw pointer avoids running consumer code from static destructors during process teardown

claims.author: sedited
claims.harm: Global logging callback leaks state across unit tests if not reset
claims.quote: Even though this function is scoped to this test, it now enables logging for all the the other unit tests too. Maybe add another call to set the callback to null at the end of the test?

status_by.quote: The `Logger` class should offer all required functionality, in a way that is much harder to abuse. Thank you both for your ideas and suggestions.

claims.status_note: author pushed an RAII Logger class wrapper preventing state leakage across tests

claims.author: sedited
claims.quote: How about calling this `logging_reset_callback` and removing the argument?
claims.request: Rename to logging_reset_callback and remove the argument

status_by.quote: I agree, but this is no longer relevant in the latest version as per https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34775#discussion_r4036445255.

claims.status_note: author agreed in concept but noted it was rendered obsolete by the new Logger wrapper design

claims.author: w0xlt
claims.harm: Tests installing global callback leak state unless explicitly cleared
claims.quote: any test that installs the global logging callback now needs to clear it before returning to prevent state leakage into later tests.

status_by.quote: The `Logger` class should offer all required functionality, in a way that is much harder to abuse.

claims.status_note: author adopted RAII wrapper approach to prevent test state leakage

claims.author: w0xlt
claims.quote: I think the C++ wrapper could retain RAII while still exposing a single global logging callback.
claims.request: Retain RAII in the C++ wrapper while exposing a single global logging callback

status_by.quote: address @w0xlt's suggestion to have an RAII `Logger` in the C++ wrapper instead of free functions

claims.status_note: author implemented an RAII Logger class in the C++ wrapper
